verdicts.reasoning: Slides 6–9 already provide teacher modelling, a coding video, an animated build GIF, and a step-by-step tutorial as concrete guided routes to the same core outcome, so the claim that only an open Extend exists is false.
The Evaluate slide contains only broad reflective questions and no observable criterion or prompt that checks whether learners understand the repeated two-frame sequence.
The Share notes give partial discussion prompts but do not supply a teacher-only convention for consistently distinguishing a valid looped animation from the specified structural errors.
Although the deck explains that forever repeats, it never contrasts this with one-time on-start execution or explicitly diagnoses the static-output misconception.
Slide 3 defines animation as a sequence of still images and slide 5 models the complete four-block sequence, already teaching the two-image-before-repeat structure required by the canonical project.
